items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: In 1955 I asked Lou Sherry if I could take leave of absence

ctx.x: That's right -- sitting around the studio. Now that show went on -- you stayed on that show until the Benny Goodman story, I think.

Right, uh huh. In 1955 I asked Lou Sherry if I could take leave of absence to work on the Benny Goodman Story for two months, since I had the offer to go out to Hollywood to do that, and Lou Sherry said that, well, this is the early days of TV, so there is no such thing as a two month leave, because in two months, there might not even be any more radio -- because nobody knew what would happen to radio; television was creating such an enormous impact on the industry, and nobody knew just the way things were going…

So I thought it'd be worthwhile to get back in the public eye, performing on the road, so I quit to do the movie, The Goodman Story, and I'd been out traveling playing from engagement to engagement ever since. After ten years in the studios, I was staying in New York all that time, primarily sticking with the radio and teaching at Juilliard or private teaching.
